CANONICAL_NAME.value: Radamsa 0.6 -- a general-purpose mutational fuzzer (Aki Helin, OUSPG), written in Owl Lisp

value.lineage: Black-box mutation fuzzing (Miller 1990 'fuzz'; Helin's Radamsa 2010-): take valid samples, apply a menu of structural mutations (byte flips, repeats, list/tree edits, number nudges) and emit adversarial inputs. Written in Owl Lisp (Helin's own purely functional Scheme dialect) and compiled to C -- a legacy-culture artifact as well as a pressure generator. PAIR: radamsa (pressure) <-> cJSON (the parser under attack).

value.built_to: manufacture inputs that are almost valid, in volume, to find where a parser breaks
value.pressure: the parser's assumptions; the human need to find crashes before attackers do
value.success_means: the emitted cases are diverse, reproducible under a seed, and reach deep parser states

value.pressure: adversarial input, the asymmetry between one parser and unbounded malformed input
value.failure_condition: mutations too shallow (all rejected at the first byte) or non-reproducible

ANCESTRY.value: Black-box mutation fuzzing (Miller 1990 'fuzz'; Helin's Radamsa 2010-): take valid samples, apply a menu of structural mutations (byte flips, repeats, list/tree edits, number nudges) and emit adversarial inputs. Written in Owl Lisp (Helin's own purely functional Scheme dialect) and compiled to C -- a legacy-culture artifact as well as a pressure generator. cut.note: a menu of 32 mutators at five representation levels (byte, byte-sequence, line, delimiter-tree, lexed string) under a scheduler whose only feedback is whether the mutation changed the bytes -- there is no signal from the target

provenance.grade_basis: Techne record nyx_handoff.where_it_came_from (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_interpretation: mutators compete for use; ones that keep producing changes get used more
organs.mechanism: each mutator carries (score in [2, 10], randomised from the seed at start; a user priority from the -m string); to pick one, draw rand(score * priority) per mutator and sort descending; try them in that order until one CHANGES the current chunk; every tried mutator returns a delta (+1 / -1 drawn with a 11/20 upward bias on success, -1 when it could not apply) which is added to its score and clamped; the new closure carries the updated scores ('always remember whatever was learned')
organs.input: the mutator list, a random state, the data stream
organs.output: a mutated stream and a re-scored mutator list
assumptions: 'the bytes changed' is the only success signal available; the delta is a biased random walk, not a reward from the target
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: prevents a stuck mutator (one that never applies to this input) from being drawn forever; the record's 'mutations too shallow' failure is what the menu, not the scheduler, addresses

organs.mechanism: a pattern decides how many mutations one output gets and where: mutate-once walks the lazy byte stream decrementing an 'inverse probability' counter drawn at start so the position is geometric-like and the last chunk is always eligible; pat-many applies once then possibly again; pat-burst applies several in a row at one place; patterns are themselves chosen by priority (mux-patterns)

organs.human_name: bd bf bi br bp bei bed ber (sed-byte-*)
organs.mechanism: edit-byte-vector at a random index: drop, flip one bit, insert random, repeat (with a heavy-tailed repeat count, repeat-len), permute a few, +1, -1, replace random; each returns the delta for the scheduler
pick a range and repeat it (repeat-len times) or delete it

organs.human_name: ld lds lr2 li lr ls lp lis lrs (line-op / stateful-line-op)
organs.mechanism: line-op wraps a generic list operation (delete, delete-sequence, duplicate, clone nearby, repeat, swap, permute) as: split the chunk on newlines -> apply -> join; stateful-line-op carries state across calls for insert/replace 'from elsewhere' (a line seen earlier)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the same list ops serve lines and (below) tree nodes: representation lifting is the design
organs.source_boundary: lines / unlines / line-op / stateful-line-op and the nine definitions

organs.mechanism: partial-parse builds a tree from balanced delimiter pairs (usual-delims: brackets, braces, quotes...; grow / count-nodes / sublists); a random subtree is deleted, duplicated, swapped with another, or a parent->child path is repeated ('stutter'); flatten writes the tree back
assumptions: the input has nested delimiters (JSON, XML, source code)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the answer to 'mutations too shallow': structure-preserving edits pass the first byte checks

organs.mechanism: string-lex splits a chunk into text / byte / delimited(quote) regions when it is 'texty enough' (6+ printable bytes); a region is mutated by inserting or overwriting known-bad strings (format specifiers, huge lengths, 'A' runs -- silly-strings) or a random lex string; string-unlex rebuilds
find digit runs, parse, replace with a boundary-ish value (the delta generators rand-delta / rand-delta-up and xp.scm's number tables -- xp.scm NOT read)

organs.human_name: ft fo fn (sed-fuse-this / fuse-old / fuse-next), fuse.scm
organs.mechanism: jump from one position to another that shares a suffix (a suffix-array style join) inside the block, with an earlier sample, or with the next -- a crossover operator between inputs (fuse.scm not read)
re-encode a code point with too many continuation bytes; insert from a table of troublesome code points (funny-unicode)

rejected_cuts.evidence: every function takes and returns rs; ll forces chunks on demand -- Owl Lisp purity discipline, not fuzzing machinery
rejected_cuts.note: it IS what makes the seed reproducible (record failure condition 'non-reproducible'); recorded as the mechanism of pressure 2, rejected as an organ

pressures.source_evidence: record pressure / failure; the mutation menu
pressures.condition: a target rejects most random bytes at the first check; the fuzzer sees nothing from the target (no crash feedback, no coverage) and must still produce inputs that reach deep code
pressures.resource_or_constraint: no target feedback; a fixed menu of edits
pressures.failure_condition: all cases rejected at the first byte (record)
pressures.world_rewards: edits at the representation level the target parses (lines, trees, strings, numbers) and a menu wide enough that some edit applies
pressures.observable_consequence: how far into cjson's parser the cases get (record entry point: pipe into cjson under ASan)
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: replay a corpus of known crashes (the world must present a new target)
pressures.cheat_control: a mutator given the target's grammar must reach deeper than every menu item; if the world scores it equal to byte flips, depth is not being measured

pressures.source_evidence: the rs threading in every function
pressures.condition: a found bug is worthless unless the input can be regenerated; every random choice must derive from one seed and nothing else (no time, no I/O order)
pressures.world_rewards: threading one random state through every decision
pressures.observable_consequence: byte-identical output for the same seed and input
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: log every output (space; the world must charge for it)

pressures.condition: some operators never apply to this input and some always change it; the only observable is whether the output differs; the choice must not starve rare operators nor waste draws on inapplicable ones
pressures.failure_condition: repeatedly drawing an operator that cannot apply
pressures.world_rewards: a self-scoring scheduler with a floor (min-score 2) so nothing starves
pressures.cheat_control: a scheduler told which operators apply must waste zero draws; if the world scores it equal to uniform, applicability is not being charged

composition_edges.label: competes
composition_edges.note: same list ops lifted to a different representation

unexplained: generators / output / fuse / xp / digest unread
the lazy-stream position walk in mutate-once is read once, not understood to the constant (initial-ip 'magic value')
the scheduler's delta is a biased random walk: whether scores ever separate mutators in practice is UNKNOWN by run
residue.note: the menu and the scheduler are fully read; the per-mutator implementations are read by index and signature
